label: No October Comey Letter
detail: The FBI director sends no late-October letter to Congress about newly found emails, so the email inquiry stays closed after July.
assumption: Late-deciding voters who were moved by the renewed email story do not see it, so the nominee's late slide is reduced and some of her lost support returns in the closing week.
facts_text: The federal investigation into the email server was closed in July with no charges recommended, and no new development has been announced since.
The final week of the campaign is dominated by other news, including the economy and the candidates' closing rallies.
nominee_news: Her campaign has been dogged for over a year by questions about her use of a private email server while she was Secretary of State.
The FBI concluded in July that no charges were warranted, and her campaign has since sought to turn the page on the matter.
research_questions: How did late-deciding voters shift when a scandal about a candidate was revived in the last two weeks of a campaign?
How much did voters' views of a candidate's honesty change after an official investigation was publicly reopened or closed?
How did turnout among a candidate's own supporters change when late news made the race look closer or less certain?
source_text: FBI Director James Comey never sends his October 28, 2016 letter to Congress.
